Siya's story

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A 9 year old girl is mauled by three pitbulls for two hours, we look at why no-one helped her

Summary:
Vusi and Wendy Khumalo are still in shock after their daughter Siya was mauled by three pitbulls last year. But the story gets worse, as it unravels. Police officers came to the house and instead of stopping the dogs they left because it was too dangerous. Neighbours walked the other way, only one neighbour eventually came across and hit one of the dogs with a hammer releasing its grip on the mauled child. The SPCA never came to put the animals down, they are still in the custody of their owners. Owners who Vusi alleges are in a dog fighting ring and this is why nobody would help and why there have been no legal repercussion for what happened to his child.
We will be interviewing the whole family, as well as the investigating officer. We are still developing the investigation part, but I am suggesting:
Confront the police department about the police man who did nothing
Confront the SAPCA as to why to the animals have not been put down, as this is the law?
Find the owners of the dogs or at least try and provide evidence that they into dog fighting or breeding fighting dogs?


Further information:
Siya Khumalo was living with her parents, Vusi and Wendy in their cottage in Rosettenville when the attack happened. They were renting a cottage from two Cameroonian men at the time, there were many pitbills living on the property at time. One afternoon Siya came home after school to find the dogs not locked up, she was immediately attacked by all three dogs. This was at 14:30
Vusi returned home at 16:30 to find his child near dead. No-one had called an ambulance. He called a taxi and rushed her to Bara where she spend 6 months. Her kidneys almost failed and eventually she got such bad septicemia that they had to amputate her leg. Wendy, Siya'a mom, had to quit her job to take care of her child reducing the families income to one salary. Siya had to be carried everywhere. Eventually one of her friends contacted the 94.7 wish list and the dischem foundation donated a prosthetic limb for Siya, as well as psychological treatment for the whole family. The trauma of watching her 9 year old child suffer so much and the financial strain it placed on the family pushed Wendy into a dark place and a few weeks ago she tried to commit suicide. What these dogs did to this family will affect them for the rest of their lives, yet the owners of these dangerous animals have gone untouched. The animals are still in their custody, which is illegal. They should have been removed. Their violent tendencies are due to the way they have been brought up and they need to more removed or put down. The SPCA has done nothing.
The owner of the dog was charged, but the case has gone nowhere.

Press Release:


Siya’s Story
Last year a 9-year-old girl was brutally mauled by her landlord’s pitbull terriers. Siya Khumalo lost her leg after the savage attack, which lasted an agonising two hours. According to witnesses, police officers at the scene failed to intervene, saying they were just too afraid. But there is renewed hope on the horizon for this young survivor. Carte Blanche follows her journey.


Script:


Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
00:03 Siya with classmates sitting on a bench and talking

Boy: What do you usually like to do?
Siya: I play with my friends and run around
Boy: What is your favourite thing?
Siya: snake and ladders
Girl: Siya what is your favourite song?
Siya: Its Justine Bieber – Is it too late to say sorry
Boy: Siya come lets hear your song


00:21 Siya and classmates sit on a bench and sing The group sings the Justin Bieber song Is it too late to say sorry
00:33 Devi stands and speaks towards camera Devi: On the 25th of May 2015 Siya Khumalo’s life was changed forever after she was viciously attached by two pit-bulls
00:44 Establish of the house were Siya was attacked by the pitbulls. Gentleman who used to stay in the residence By the time when the accident happened I was staying in this house, there are alloy of tenants at the back and the landlord is staying in the main house. The dogs used to stay in this garage where they keep their store inside there
00:55 Devi interviews Siyas father about what happened. Devi: So these dogs were like a security force for the stock for that spaza shop?
Vusi: Yeah for the store
01:04 Walking shot of Siya explaining what happened to her when she got attached. Music in the background V/O Siya: I was walking back from school then I came home. Then I opened the gate and locked it, then I went to the back yard then I saw two pit-bull. One dog grabbed my bag then I fell down…
Siya on screen: Then the other dog bit my leg then I screamed for help
01:33 Mkhay the neighbour explains what he saw and happened to Siya


Montage of Mkhay explaining what he did Mkhay: I just hear the voice of girl crying, I think yah the mother is beating the girl then he just called me “ahh the dog is biting the child” then I run to the gate I saw police car was just parking there in the intersection. I just called those police and they run and came here but they didn’t do anything.

They were scared of those dogs then I run to my house then I take a hammer, I jumped through next door then I grabbed one of those dogs I hit them in the head. Because that big dog, black one they want to come and bite him
02:17 Siya on a swing and VO V/O : To this day the SAPS have not managed to locate the Officers that were too scared to help save Siya that day. After knocking one of the dogs unconcious Mkay managed to protect Siya until the owners returned and took the dogs away.
02:32 Siya sitting on the couch speaking about what happened Siya: I never felt anything, but the only thing I felt I was tired.
-Siya cries-
02:48 VO of Devi. Siya continues crying as Devi wipes her tears Various neigbours tried to call for an Abulance, but after waiting for over 2 hours no abulance arrived.
02:52 Siya's father, Vusi Khumalo speaks about what happened that Vusi: I found my daughter lying, full of blood around her and the landlord and his brother were sitting with Siya. Siya didn’t say anything I see was losing power and didn’t talk didn’t do anything I just see his eyes she still alive but can’t say thing to me. I asked one of my next door with a car to just take my daughter to the nearest hospital
03:23 Devi and Vusi sitting down and talking. Interview Devi: What are the Doctors saying to you?
Vusi: The doctor just says the condition of Siya is getting worse instead of getting better. So they say they will continue trying because she went to theatre almost six times, after that they said “there’s no other way only cut”, they said its about saving the life because in the first place they were trying to save her leg.


03:51 Siya speaks of her memory of what happened when she found out that her leg had been cut off. She speaks with Devi on the couch. Siya: I asked my mother “Mom where is my leg? “ then she said “you saw baby girl that leg had injured and they put it in the freezer” then I said “Okay when am I going to get my leg back? “ and then she said ”you wont get your leg back nana”

04:15 Montage of Siya and her mother, Wendy Khumalo while she bathes her. Wendy: Sometimes it makes me scared but sometimes it doesn’t. But when she saw a dog she was screaming, she was terrible to me but I’m trying to cope now because I have to wash her I have to help to do everything she can’t do herself. If I go I have to go with her I can’t leave her alone here.

04:54 Siya and Wendy sit in the room while she baths and speak with regards to her fears Siya: When I’m alone I think dogs will come, something like that.
05:01 Siya gets dressed montage and V/O V/O: Directly after the attach the owner of the dog signed away 1 of the 2 pit-bull to the Animal Anti Cruelty League but according to the animals protection act its is the responsibility of the SAPS to obtain a warrant to have an animal removed if it has caused injury to another person. Yet one of the pit-bull that attacked Siya is still on this property where 3 other 10-year-old children live. We contacted the SAPS for a statement but they declined to comment.
05:30 Devi speaking to camera Devi: So after an entire year of no action from either the police or the NSPCA we contacted the Soweto Animal Rescue and Advisory centre. Jerry from that organisation acted immediately he went to court he got a warrant and now has access to the premises
05:47 Jerry Selwane speaks to Devi outside the premises of the Dogs house. Jerry: We need to gain access you know to remove this animal, which is deemed to be very aggressive. It was decided this morning that we should come and remove the remaining animal and take it to a place of safety.
06:04 Knocking on the premises. Captain Novela: We are the police if you don’t open for us we are going to break everything down.
Owner of the dog: Its up to you, you can break it. If I open for them they will fight me you know.
06:19 VO with Captain Novela going to issue a warrant V/O: Captian Novela from the SAPS is here to issue a warrant to have the dog removed from the property.
06:24 POV of Devi and the warrant Devi: so this warrant basically gives the police…
Captain Novela: gives the power to remove the dogs from the premises.
Devi: and it was requested do you know when?
Jerry: This morning.
Devi: So you went to court this morning so it’s a fresh warrant?
Captain Novela: it’s a fresh warrant
Devi: explain to us how does it work? Like what are the correct procedures in the future?
Captain Novela: No we not allowed to talk to the media either

06:49 VO Devi. Men brining the dog out After repeated phone calls Theo Kempo, The owner of the dogs that attacked Siya, returned home.
06:54 Two men bring out the pit-bull. They are instructed to put it in the car. Captain Novela: aha don’t bring it to me put it in that car

Jerry: Look the dog looks very nervous; you can see the lack of human interaction with this animal. And the way the guy was dragging the animal you can see that they hardly walk this dog. You can see they don’t even walk this dog. The dog was kept for safe guarding as a security and by law for you to keep any animal for safe guarding you need to have a permit and a license to keep such things,
07:32 Devi speaks to the Theo the dog owner Devi: how did you feel when this happened to Vusi’s daughter?
Theo: I swear to God I never knew that something like that can happen, it could’ve happened to my own son
07:40 Theo Kempo the dog owner explains why the dog was kept in the yard.

Theo speaks to Jerry and Devi Theo: this dog was there to protect us against this broken house, people jumping in my yard every time
Jerry: So the dogs were purely here to guard your property?
Theo: Yes…
Jerry: that’s where the problem is, the dog was never walked
Theo: No no no no…
Jerry: You can see, I mean it doesn’t take a genius to see. You saw how he was dragging the dog and you saw how the dog was terrified the tale was between the legs
Devi: I mean the dog is going away you don’t even say good bye you don’t even look emotionally upset, are you?
Theo: I’m stopping it here…
08:17 Theo signs some papers with Jerry and goes back into his house Jerry: What I can tell you there’s nothing wrong with pit-bull, pit-bull become a dangerous weapon when they are in the wrong hands
08:22 V/O explaining the conclusion Devi: Theo Kempo the owner of the pit-bull that attacked Siya is being charged with assault which holds a minimum of three years his due to appear in court on the 14th of April.
08:33 Devi concludes to camera Devi: A year after the incident through various donors, Siya is being fitted for a prosthetic limb which will allow her to try and live a normal life.
08:47 Siya and family meet Dr Roger Wolfson the prosthesis Roger: Hello Siya
Siya: hello.
Roger: Today we are going to have our first fitting, so now we are going to do a weight bearing, put your weight on a jig and we going to get a height reading. How is that feeling Siya?
Siya: its fine
Roger: Hurting you?
Siya: No
Roger: Promise?
Siya: Promise
Roger: In the beginning she going to have to go through a few prosthetic sockets because the stump is going to keep shrinking its going to have a loss of volume its going to move around and cause shafting and hurting. In the first year I foresee a strong girl like this she going to go through at least about two to three sockets the cost here for the family is between R500 000– R700 000 in the next 5 years.
09:39 Siya speaks of how she feels with getting the prosthetic leg Siya: I feel happy because I will be able to walk again and play with other children.

09:47 Walking into the sunlight with her family Devi: what do you want to be when you grow up?
Siya: I want to be a doctor
I want to help other peoples lives as they help my life

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A 9 year old girl is mauled by three pitbulls for two hours, we look at why no-one helped her
metadata.Summary: Vusi and Wendy Khumalo are still in shock after their daughter Siya was mauled by three pitbulls last year. But the story gets worse, as it unravels. Police officers came to the house and instead of stopping the dogs they left because it was too dangerous. Neighbours walked the other way, only one neighbour eventually came across and hit one of the dogs with a hammer releasing its grip on the mauled child. The SPCA never came to put the animals down, they are still in the custody of their owners. Owners who Vusi alleges are in a dog fighting ring and this is why nobody would help and why there have been no legal repercussion for what happened to his child. We will be interviewing the whole family, as well as the investigating officer. We are still developing the investigation part, but I am suggesting: Confront the police department about the police man who did nothing Confront the SAPCA as to why to the animals have not been put down, as this is the law? Find the owners of the dogs or at least try and provide evidence that they into dog fighting or breeding fighting dogs?
metadata.Further information: Siya Khumalo was living with her parents, Vusi and Wendy in their cottage in Rosettenville when the attack happened. They were renting a cottage from two Cameroonian men at the time, there were many pitbills living on the property at time. One afternoon Siya came home after school to find the dogs not locked up, she was immediately attacked by all three dogs. This was at 14:30 Vusi returned home at 16:30 to find his child near dead. No-one had called an ambulance. He called a taxi and rushed her to Bara where she spend 6 months. Her kidneys almost failed and eventually she got such bad septicemia that they had to amputate her leg. Wendy, Siya'a mom, had to quit her job to take care of her child reducing the families income to one salary. Siya had to be carried everywhere. Eventually one of her friends contacted the 94.7 wish list and the dischem foundation donated a prosthetic limb for Siya, as well as psychological treatment for the whole family. The trauma of watching her 9 year old child suffer so much and the financial strain it placed on the family pushed Wendy into a dark place and a few weeks ago she tried to commit suicide. What these dogs did to this family will affect them for the rest of their lives, yet the owners of these dangerous animals have gone untouched. The animals are still in their custody, which is illegal. They should have been removed. Their violent tendencies are due to the way they have been brought up and they need to more removed or put down. The SPCA has done nothing. The owner of the dog was charged, but the case has gone nowhere.
